commitResults.messageTitle: Add relationships and remove address support
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts currently track addresses but do not distinguish clients from prospects. Replace address handling with a relationship category and accept it with r/ when adding contacts.

Keep tag editing available while add leaves tag input disabled.

Phone fields currently reject useful formatting and labels, while their error message does not identify the reason for rejection.

Accept phone-like eight-digit sequences with ordinary separators and labels. Report specific validation errors and update affected test data.

Name validation currently permits digits but excludes customary punctuation and relationship markers.

Allow letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and recognized relationship markers. Enforce the required trimmed length and reject arbitrary slash usage.

Email validation currently reports a generic format error, which makes correction difficult.

Validate practical email formats with common local-part characters and provide specific errors for invalid email parts.

The add command currently returns generic errors for missing fields, and the guide does not describe the refined input rules.

Report actionable add errors, distinguish overlong names, and document the name and email formats.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect duplicate contacts by email or phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts currently use names as their identity, even though names can be incomplete or shared.

Treat matching email addresses or phone numbers as duplicate contacts and report the matching field when adding.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify name and phone validation errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Validation errors currently show more detail than users need for invalid names and incomplete phone numbers.

Report concise messages for invalid name characters and incomplete phone numbers while retaining separate blank and length errors.
Add client financial information value types

Email addresses without a dotted domain are accepted even though ClientBook targets public-facing contact records.

Require a dot in the domain and document the rule.

The use cases contain inconsistent formatting and the requirements omit relevant project constraints.

Standardize the use-case layout and add the missing requirements.

The minimum length still permits addresses that cannot contain a dotted domain after public-domain validation was introduced.

Raise the minimum length and align the tests with current rules.
Wrap long client financial information

The edit command cannot change a contact's relationship status, even though it is required when adding a contact.

Allow optional relationship-status edits with the same validation as add, and document and test the expanded command.

Backup and restore still reference removed AddressBook storage types.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix backup and restore data safety
commitResults.messageBody:
Backups can overwrite a valid copy before a new write completes, and a
failed restore can leave the displayed records out of sync with storage.

Write backups through a temporary sibling file, persist restored records
before updating the model, and derive backup locations from configured
storage. Require callers to provide storage explicitly.

Restore already persists its data before mutating the model, but LogicManager saves it again after command execution. Mark persisted command results so LogicManager skips that second write, and verify the restore path saves once.
Phone duplicates currently depend on formatting and allow numbers longer than the E.164 limit. Compare complete number sequences, enforce the 15-digit maximum, and document the rules.
Email domains with different casing currently bypass duplicate detection. Normalize domain casing for equality, preserve local-part casing, and document the rule.

The edit-command branch removes backup and restore parser routes inherited from master, leaving the restore integration test unable to parse its command. Restore both routes and their coverage, and revert model changes when a save fails so the displayed records remain consistent with persisted data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Roll back changes after failed saves
commitResults.messageBody: A failed persistence operation leaves the in-memory client book and its filtered view changed even though the data is not saved. Restore both states after a failed save and show one actionable message for all save failures.

Read-only commands attempt to save unchanged records, so they fail when storage is unavailable. Save only changed client-book data, document the behavior, and verify that list does not write to storage.

Client data currently follows the launch directory, which creates a separate list when the JAR is run elsewhere.

Resolve storage paths from the application JAR directory so each launch uses the same client data and preferences.

Email validation accepts labels longer than DNS permits.

Reject labels over 63 characters for both commands and document the limit in the User Guide.

Log files currently follow the launch directory, which leaves portable-app files split across folders.

Resolve the log file path from the application JAR directory so logs travel with the application.
The add command previously accepted tags and reported missing fields individually. Remove tag handling and present the concise required-parameter format for incomplete commands.
Add and edit commands previously allowed contacts to share a name. Reject name conflicts while retaining the existing email and phone duplicate checks.

Commands now run against a temporary model and the visible model updates only after persistence succeeds. Preserve the active filter across the temporary-model commit and cover a failed save followed by a successful tag.
